newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ privatisation target GPS reports yr profit jump.
newsitem.headline: NZ privatisation target GPS reports yr profit jump.

text.p: New Zealand's state-owned property company GPS, slated for possible float in last week's budget, on Thursday reported a sharp jump in post-tax profits for the year to March and made forecasts for future earnings.

In its annual report and statement of corporate intent, tabled in parliament during the morning, the company said it had made a net profit of NZ$23.4 million including a revaluation gain of $6.4 million.
It paid the government a $12 million dividend, and said in its statement of future performance targets that the board proposed a similar level of dividend in 1997/98.

The Government Property Services' board predicted that net profit before interest, tax and revaluations, as a percentage of shareholders' funds, would be 14.1 percent in the year to March 1998, dipping to 13.5 percent the following year then rising to 14 percent in 2000.
Its expected vacancy rate next year would be 5.0 percent, it added.
During the reporting year GPS sold three properties from its portfolio for a gross $9.3 million, leaving it with 35 on its books at the balance date.

In his comments in the annual report, chairman Colin Beyer said, "After turbulent times in the first four years, the company has been successfully restructured and is now performing as well as, and generally better than, most private sector property investment companies.

"Shareholders now stand to gain the benefits of owning a company with a well-leased, well-maintained and professionally-managed portfolio of office property financed competitively and with prospects that property values will continue to improve," he added.
GPS said that after a series of funding changes during the year, including a bond refinance, the company now has a fixed annual funding cost for the next four years of 7.8 percent.
In a press statement released later, Beyer said the outlook for property leasing was strong in Wellington but continued to be difficult in some regions.
GPS's Wellington portfolio dominates its books, representing 82 percent of the total by value, and currently less than two percent of it is vacant.
While rental rates for prime office space in Wellington now range between $225 and $315 gross per square metre, forecasters predict they will rise to $380 to $490 by 2000, GPS noted.
For the next three or four years the outlook for property values "remains encouraging", Beyer added.
"Most commentators suggest that the office property market is likely to continue upwards in the current growth phase, which began in most sectors in the 1994/95 year," he said.

The Herald newspaper reported that moves towards a float are proceeding apace, with sharebrokers having been asked to enter submissions by July 14 for the first stage of a float which could be carried out by the end of this year.
It was not immediately possible to confirm this report.
